@frontend-design:frontend-design @gsd-manager @gsd-review-backlog @gsd-new-project @gsd-explore @gsd-import @gsd-list-workspaces @gsd-ui-phase @gsd-cleanup @gsd-do @omc-reference @gsd-list-phase-assumptions @gsd-thread @gsd-add-todo @gsd-secure-phase @gsd-code-review-fix @gsd-resume-work @gsd-audit-fix @gsd-forensics @gsd-verify-work @gsd-note @gsd-audit-fix @gsd-verify-work @gsd-validate-phase @gsd-progress @gsd-debug @gsd-analyze-dependencies @gsd-autonomous @gsd-code-review @writer-memory @debug @self-improve @autopilot @remember @team @omc-teams @ultrawork @verify @subagent-driven-development @requesting-code-review @gsd-code-review-fix @gsd-code-review @autopilot @agent-analyst @agent-bug-analyzer @agent-bug-analyzer @ @agent-designer @agent-gsd-security-auditor @agent-security-reviewer @agent-dev-planner Perform a comprehensive end-to-end audit and systematic fix of the entire Next.js codebase to ensure the application builds, runs, and operates with zero errors out of the box, with a strong emphasis on real-time data synchronization, strict user isolation, and robust security.

Before starting, confirm the project root directory and the package manager being used (npm, yarn, or pnpm). For each area, output a summary of findings before making changes so I can review the plan.

Area 1: Frontend-Backend Communication and Real-Time Data Synchronization
Locate all API route handlers by scanning the app/api directory and pages/api directory. For each route file, identify the expected HTTP methods and the request body or query parameter shapes by reading the handler code. Then search the entire codebase for fetch calls, SWR hooks, React Query queries, and Next.js data fetching methods that call those endpoints. Build a mapping of every client call to its corresponding server handler. For each pair, verify the endpoint URL matches the file path, the HTTP method matches, the request payload shape matches what the handler parses from req.body or req.query, and the response JSON shape matches what the client code destructures or accesses. Fix any mismatches by updating either the client or server to align. Implement real-time data synchronization across the application. Establish WebSocket connections or integrate a real-time library (such as Socket.io, Supabase realtime, or Firebase) for all dynamic data. Ensure that database updates, AI function results, and API state changes propagate instantly to the client without requiring manual page refreshes. Add proper error handling to any endpoint that lacks a try-catch block. Check that Date objects are serialized as ISO strings and deserialized back to Date on the client, that undefined values are handled since JSON omits them, and that nested objects survive serialization. After fixing, list each endpoint and its corrected client-handler pair along with its real-time update mechanism.

Area 2: Caching Optimization
For every page in the app directory, determine whether it uses server components, client components, or a mix. For each page, decide the optimal rendering strategy based on the nature of its data. Pages with content that updates occasionally but does not need real-time freshness should use ISR by exporting a revalidate value in seconds. Pages that must always show the latest data should use SSR by forcing dynamic rendering with export const dynamic equals force-dynamic. Pages with highly dynamic client-side data should use CSR with SWR or React Query and an appropriate refresh interval. For every API route, add Cache-Control headers to the response based on the data sensitivity. Use revalidatePath or revalidateTag after any mutation to purge stale caches. Check for and fix any issues where cached authentication state could leak between users, particularly in middleware or getServerSideProps. After fixing, output a table listing each page and its assigned rendering strategy with the specific revalidation time or refresh interval.

Area 3: Next.js Performance Optimization
Use the Next.js bundle analyzer or inspect the build output to identify the largest JavaScript bundles and the components contributing to them. For each heavy component such as chart libraries, rich text editors, large data tables, and third-party widgets, wrap it in a dynamic import using next/dynamic with ssr set to false where the component does not render on the server, and add a meaningful loading placeholder. Audit every img tag across the project and convert each one to the next/image component with explicit width, height, and descriptive alt attributes. Add Suspense boundaries around independent data-fetching sections of pages to enable streaming SSR. Review the metadata export on every page and ensure each one includes a title, description, and Open Graph tags for social sharing. Inspect the middleware file for any heavy computation or blocking operations and refactor to keep it lightweight for edge runtime. Measure the total bundle size before starting this area and again after all changes, then report the difference.

Area 4: Error Handling and Edge Cases
Search the entire codebase for all async operations including fetch calls, database queries, file system reads, and external API integrations. Wrap each one in a try-catch block that catches specific error types where possible and falls back to a generic error handler. Create a reusable ErrorBoundary React component that accepts a fallback prop and place it at strategic levels in the component tree, specifically around each major page section, around data-dependent components, and around third-party integrations. Define a consistent error response format that includes a user-friendly message string, a machine-readable error code string, and a unique correlation ID for log correlation. Add a loading skeleton or spinner component to every async operation so the user sees feedback while waiting. Create an empty state component and add it to every list and table that could receive zero items. Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for network requests and add an offline indicator component that shows when the browser detects no network connection. Search for unhandled promise rejections by finding floating await expressions inside non-async functions, .then chains without a .catch handler, and event handlers that call async functions without catching errors.

Area 5: Full Functionality Audit, AI Integration, and Database Integrity
Enumerate every page route by scanning the file system for page.tsx, page.jsx, and pages directory files. For each route, attempt to render it and log any runtime errors. For every interactive element on each page, trace the complete chain from the DOM event through the handler function to the state update or API call and verify each step executes correctly. For every form, verify that client-side validation exists, that the submission handler wraps the API call in try-catch, that the success state renders a confirmation message or redirect, and that the error state renders the validation or server errors to the user. Walk through the complete authentication flow by tracing the login form submission to the session creation to the protected route middleware check to the logout function and session destruction. For every CRUD resource in the application, verify the list view renders items, the create form submits and adds the item, the update form pre-fills and saves changes, and the delete confirmation removes the item. Audit all AI functions and integrations by verifying that prompts are correctly formatted, API keys are securely managed, responses are properly parsed and validated, and streaming responses are handled correctly without breaking the UI. Audit all database interactions by verifying that connection pooling is configured, queries use parameterized statements to prevent SQL injection, transactions are used where multiple writes must succeed or fail together, and schema migrations are up to date. Ensure all database reads and writes reflect immediately in the application UI through the real-time mechanisms established in Area 1.

Area 6: Code Quality, Security, and Strict User Isolation
Search the entire codebase for console.log, console.warn, console.error, console.info, console.debug, and debugger statements using grep or ripgrep. Remove every instance or replace it with a proper logging utility that respects the environment and can be silenced in production. Run the TypeScript compiler with strict mode enabled and capture the full output. Fix every compilation error by updating types, adding type annotations, or refactoring code. Search for all instances of the any type and replace each one with a proper type definition that accurately describes the data shape. Create or verify a centralized environment variable configuration module that reads from process.env, provides fallback values for optional variables, and throws a clear descriptive error at application startup when any required variable is missing. Implement strict user isolation at the code level. Audit every database query, API route, and server action to ensure it includes a user ID filter derived from the authenticated session so no user can access or modify another user's data. Implement Row Level Security (RLS) if using a supported database like PostgreSQL or Supabase. Sanitize all user inputs to prevent XSS and injection attacks. Add rate limiting to all public API routes and authentication endpoints. Verify that CORS policies are strict and that sensitive environment variables are never exposed to the client. Verify that error handling follows the same pattern across all files with consistent error classes, response formats, and logging.

After completing all six areas, run the build command for the project (next build or the appropriate build script from package.json) and capture the full terminal output. If the build fails with any errors or warnings, fix each one and rebuild. Repeat this cycle until the build completes with a clean exit code of zero and no errors. Then start the production server and verify that the home page loads correctly in the browser. Navigate to at least five additional key pages that represent core functionality and verify each one renders without console errors and that interactive elements respond correctly. Test real-time features by triggering database updates and verifying the UI updates automatically. Test user isolation by logging in as two different users simultaneously and confirming neither can see the other's data.

Provide a final summary report organized by the six areas above. For each area, list every change made with the file path and a description of what was changed. List any remaining issues that could not be fully resolved with an explanation of why.
